traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Cistaceae: leaves usually opposite, sometimes whorled, rarely alternate; leaves simple; veins single, pinnate or palmate; stipules present or absent; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers solitary or in cymes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule; stamens (3-) 15 to 100; carpels 3 to 10. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
